body:
India's geographical position

India occupies a central position in South Asia. It lies entirely in the Northern Hemisphere and the Eastern Hemisphere. The Indian peninsula extends southwards into the Indian Ocean, with the Arabian Sea to its west and the Bay of Bengal to its east.

India's geographical position provides access to maritime routes connecting West Asia, Africa, Southeast Asia and Europe. The Himalayas form a major natural barrier in the north, while the surrounding seas influence rainfall, temperature, trade and coastal settlement.

Geographical featureExtent or value
Mainland latitudinal extent8°4′ N to 37°6′ N
Longitudinal extent68°7′ E to 97°25′ E
North-south extentApproximately 3,214 km
East-west extentApproximately 2,933 km
Geographical areaApproximately 3.28 million sq. km
World rank by area7th
Share of world land areaApproximately 2.4%

The conventional northern extent includes territory claimed by India. Actual administrative control and the official territorial extent are not identical in every northern border region.

Important geographical extremities

LocationGeographical association
Indira PointSouthernmost point of India; Great Nicobar Island
KanyakumariSouthernmost point of mainland India; Tamil Nadu
Western KachchhWesternmost part of India; Gujarat
Eastern Arunachal PradeshEasternmost part of India

Indira Point lies at approximately 6°45′ N latitude. It is farther south than Kanyakumari because India's national territory includes islands as well as the mainland.

The Tropic of Cancer

The Tropic of Cancer lies at approximately 23°30′ N latitude and passes through the central part of India. It separates the area in which the midday Sun can be directly overhead during part of the year from areas farther north where this does not occur.

From west to east, the Tropic of Cancer crosses 8 Indian states:

  1. Gujarat
  2. Rajasthan
  3. Madhya Pradesh
  4. Chhattisgarh
  5. Jharkhand
  6. West Bengal
  7. Tripura
  8. Mizoram

It does not pass through Maharashtra, Odisha, Bihar, Assam or Meghalaya. These states are useful points of comparison because they lie near states crossed by the Tropic of Cancer.

The Standard Meridian of India

India follows a common standard time despite its considerable east-west extent. The Standard Meridian of India is 82°30′ E longitude. Indian Standard Time is 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Coordinated Universal Time, or UTC.

The Standard Meridian passes near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh and crosses Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh from north to south.

The difference in longitude between western Gujarat and eastern Arunachal Pradesh produces a difference of approximately 2 hours in local solar time. Sunrise therefore occurs considerably earlier in eastern India, although both regions follow Indian Standard Time.

Latitude and longitude are different

The Tropic of Cancer is a line of latitude running east-west. The Standard Meridian is a line of longitude running north-south. Gujarat is crossed by the Tropic of Cancer but not by India's Standard Meridian.

Using geographical directions

Latitude determines how far north or south of the Equator a place lies. Longitude determines how far east or west of the Prime Meridian it lies. A political boundary identifies an administrative unit, whereas a physical boundary may follow a mountain range, river, desert or coastline.

Geographical relationships can be understood through relative positions. Gujarat lies west of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan lies north of Gujarat, and Maharashtra lies to its south and southeast.

Prelims focus

  • India lies in the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres.
  • The Tropic of Cancer crosses 8 Indian states.
  • The Standard Meridian is 82°30′ E.
  • Indian Standard Time is UTC + 5:30.
  • India is the 7th-largest country by geographical area.
  • Trap: Indira Point, not Kanyakumari, is the southernmost point of India's entire territory.

[Sources: NCERT, Class 6, The Earth: Our Habitat, 2018–19 edition, Maps and Our Country – India; NCERT, Class 11, India: Physical Environment, Chapter 1, India – Location, SATHEE online textbook; GCERT, Class 9, Social Science, Chapter 13, India: Location, Geological Structure and Physiography-I, pp. 99–105, online textbook copy. Online copies used where compendium text extraction was unreadable; consulted 27 November 2026.]
title: India's Location, Extent and Important Geographical Lines

body:
Political divisions of India

India consists of states and Union Territories. These are administrative divisions and should not be confused with physical regions such as the Himalayas, the Deccan Plateau or the coastal plains. A single physical region may extend across several states.

As of 27 November 2026, India has 28 states and 8 Union Territories. New Delhi is the national capital.

The traditional term Seven Sister States refers to Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura. Sikkim belongs to the wider northeastern region but is not one of the original Seven Sisters.

The 8 Union Territories

Union TerritoryCapital or administrative headquarters

DelhiDelhi

PuducherryPuducherry

Chandigarh is a Union Territory as well as the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana. Puducherry consists of geographically separated regions: Puducherry and Karaikal near Tamil Nadu, Mahe near Keralam, and Yanam within coastal Andhra Pradesh.

Administrative changes relevant to examinations

  • Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014.
  • Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh became separate Union Territories on 31 October 2019.
  • Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu were merged into one Union Territory on 26 January 2020.
  • Port Blair was renamed Sri Vijaya Puram on 13 September 2024.
  • The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026, enacted on 6 April 2026, established Amaravati as the statutory capital of Andhra Pradesh with effect deemed from 2 June 2024.
  • The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026, enacted on 14 August 2026, changed the official state name from Kerala to Keralam with effect from 25 August 2026.

These administrative changes do not alter the underlying geographical relationships. Older textbooks may use Kerala, Port Blair, Hyderabad as a shared capital, or the earlier number of states and Union Territories.

Prelims focus

  • Rajasthan is India's largest state by area; Goa is its smallest.
  • India has 28 states and 8 Union Territories at the stated cutoff.
  • Chandigarh is the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana.
  • Amaravati is the capital of Andhra Pradesh.
  • Keralam became the official state name on 25 August 2026.
  • Trap: Sri Vijaya Puram is the renamed Port Blair, not a newly established island capital.

[Sources: NCERT, Class 6, The Earth: Our Habitat, 2018–19 edition, Our Country – India and Appendix I, used for geographical foundations; National Portal of India, States and Union Territories directory; Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019; Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (Merger of Union Territories) Act, 2019; PIB, Ministry of Home Affairs, renaming of Port Blair, 13 September 2024; Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026, Act 7 of 2026, Sections 1–2; Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026, Act 18 of 2026, Sections 1, 3 and 6, commencement notification S.O. 4712(E), 25 August 2026. Administrative status checked against these sources on 27 November 2026.]
title: States, Union Territories and Their Regional Locations

body:
India's land neighbours

India's international boundaries extend across plains, deserts, mountains and river valleys. Under India's official territorial position, it shares land boundaries with 7 countries. Sri Lanka and the Maldives are important neighbouring island countries but do not share a land boundary with India.

CountryIndian states and Union Territories bordering it
PakistanGujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh
ChinaLadakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh
NepalUttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Sikkim
BhutanSikkim, West Bengal, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh
BangladeshWest Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
MyanmarArunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram
AfghanistanLadakh, under India's official territorial claim

India's official Afghanistan boundary lies in territory claimed by India but not presently under Indian administration. It must therefore be distinguished from an ordinary administered international frontier.

Bangladesh shares the longest international land boundary with India. According to the Ministry of Home Affairs boundary listing updated on 26 November 2026, its length is 4,096.70 km.

States bordering multiple countries

StateInternational neighbours
SikkimNepal, China, Bhutan
Arunachal PradeshBhutan, China, Myanmar
West BengalNepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh
UttarakhandChina, Nepal
AssamBhutan, Bangladesh
MizoramBangladesh, Myanmar

Important relationships in northeastern India

Assam occupies a central position in the Northeast. It shares boundaries with all 6 of the other traditional Seven Sister States. It also borders West Bengal.

  • Sikkim shares its only domestic state boundary with West Bengal.
  • Meghalaya shares its only domestic state boundary with Assam.
  • Tripura shares domestic boundaries with Assam and Mizoram.
  • Nagaland borders Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Manipur.
  • Manipur borders Nagaland, Assam and Mizoram.
  • Mizoram borders Assam, Manipur and Tripura.

The Siliguri Corridor is a narrow geographical connection in northern West Bengal between the main Indian landmass and northeastern India. Nepal lies to its west and Bangladesh to its south and east, with Bhutan farther northeast.

Important interstate relationships elsewhere

  • Uttar Pradesh borders 8 states: Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Bihar. It also borders Delhi.
  • Goa shares land boundaries with Maharashtra and Karnataka.
  • Keralam shares land boundaries with Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
  • Telangana is an inland state surrounded by Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.
  • Jharkhand lies south of Bihar and has no international boundary or coastline.
  • Madhya Pradesh borders Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Gujarat.

Gujarat's boundaries

Gujarat occupies the western part of India. Its geographical position connects the desert and semi-arid regions of northwestern India with the western coast and the Peninsular Plateau.

DirectionNeighbouring region
North and northeastRajasthan
EastMadhya Pradesh
South and southeastMaharashtra
NorthwestPakistan
West and southwestArabian Sea

Gujarat also shares boundaries with parts of the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh are its 3 neighbouring states.

Gujarat and Rajasthan both border Pakistan, but Rajasthan is landlocked while Gujarat has a coastline. Gujarat does not share a boundary with Goa, Haryana or Chhattisgarh.

Prelims focus

  • Bangladesh shares India's longest international land boundary.
  • Arunachal Pradesh borders Bhutan, China and Myanmar.
  • Mizoram borders both Bangladesh and Myanmar.
  • The Siliguri Corridor is in West Bengal.
  • Gujarat borders Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.
  • Trap: Meghalaya borders Bangladesh but not Myanmar.

[Sources: Ministry of Home Affairs, Border Management-I Division, country-wise international boundary listing, updated 26 November 2026; National Portal of India, States and Union Territories directory; NCERT, Class 11, India: Physical Environment, Chapter 1; GCERT, Class 9, Social Science, Chapter 13, pp. 99–105; Government of Gujarat, Narmada, Water Resources, Water Supply and Kalpsar Department, Brief Note on Water Resources Related Issues. Online sources consulted 27 November 2026.]
title: International Boundaries and Important Interstate Relationships

body:
Major physical divisions of India

India can be divided into 6 broad physiographic regions: the Himalayan mountains, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands. Physiographic divisions are based on relief, geological structure and the development of landforms rather than administrative boundaries.

The Himalayan mountain system

The Himalayas are geologically young fold mountains formed through the convergence of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates. They extend along northern India and contain high mountain ranges, glaciers, deep valleys and passes. Many major northern rivers originate in or receive water from these mountains.

Parallel Himalayan ranges

RangeRelative positionCharacteristics
Himadri or Greater HimalayaNorthernmost main Himalayan rangeVery high peaks and extensive snowfields
Himachal or Lesser HimalayaSouth of HimadriMountain valleys and hill stations
Shiwalik or Outer HimalayaSouthernmost Himalayan rangeLower foothills and unconsolidated sediments

The Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar are important ranges associated with the Lesser Himalaya. Longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwalik are called duns. Dehradun is a familiar example.

Regional divisions from west to east

The Himalayas can also be divided into longitudinal regions using major rivers as boundaries. These regional divisions are different from the north-south division into Himadri, Himachal and Shiwalik.

Regional divisionApproximate river boundaries
Punjab HimalayaIndus to Sutlej
Kumaon HimalayaSutlej to Kali
Nepal HimalayaKali to Teesta
Assam HimalayaTeesta to Dihang

These are conventional physical-geography regions. The term Punjab Himalaya, for example, does not mean that the entire region lies within the present administrative state of Punjab.

The Trans-Himalayan region

The Trans-Himalayan mountain system lies to the north of the main Himalayan ranges. Important ranges include the Karakoram, Ladakh and Zanskar ranges.

  • The Karakoram contains very high peaks and major glaciers, including the Siachen Glacier.
  • The Ladakh region contains extensive high-altitude cold desert landscapes.
  • The Zanskar region lies south of much of the Indus Valley in Ladakh.

Kanchenjunga lies along the Sikkim-Nepal boundary. Nanda Devi lies in Uttarakhand. Mount Everest lies on the Nepal-China boundary and is not situated in India.

The eastern Himalayan bend and Purvanchal

Near the eastern end of the Himalayas, the mountain system bends southwards. The hills extending through northeastern India form part of the Purvanchal or eastern hill system.

The Patkai hills, Naga Hills, Manipur hills and Mizo Hills are important components. Their general alignment differs from the predominantly east-west orientation of the main Himalayan ranges.

The Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills of Meghalaya lie south of the Brahmaputra Valley. Geologically, the Meghalaya Plateau is an extension of the ancient Peninsular Plateau rather than part of the young Himalayan mountain system.

Distinguishing adjacent regions

The Himalayas and the Meghalaya Plateau are both located in northern or northeastern India, but they differ in geological origin. The Meghalaya Plateau belongs to the older peninsular geological block.

Prelims focus

  • Himadri, Himachal and Shiwalik occur broadly from north to south.
  • Dehradun is an example of a dun valley.
  • The Karakoram belongs to the Trans-Himalayan system.
  • Kanchenjunga lies along the Sikkim-Nepal boundary.
  • Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills are in Meghalaya.
  • Trap: The Meghalaya Plateau is not a subdivision of the Greater Himalaya.

[Sources: NCERT, Class 9, Contemporary India-I, Chapter 2, Physical Features of India; NCERT, Class 11, India: Physical Environment, Chapter 2, Structure and Physiography, SATHEE online textbook; NCERT, Class 6, The Earth: Our Habitat, 2018–19 edition, Our Country – India, pp. 50–55; GCERT, Class 9, Social Science, Chapter 14, India: Location, Geological Structure and Physiography-II, pp. 106–113. Online textbooks consulted 27 November 2026.]
title: The Himalayas, Trans-Himalayan Ranges and Northeastern Hills
